[[START OF PAGE 1]]

Exterior photograph of Sir John Soane’s Museum, showing a multi-storey brick-and-stone townhouse façade with tall arched windows, a pale central section, and a black metal railing along the street.

# Sir John

Soane's

Museum

SIR JOHN
SOANE'S
MUSEUM
LONDON

Painted portrait of a seated man in dark formal clothing, associated with Sir John Soane’s Museum.

Photo of a person holding an open easy-read booklet labeled “easy read” and “Easy words and pictures.”

easy read
guide

Interior photograph from Sir John Soane’s Museum showing a dark wood-paneled room with many small decorative objects and plaques on the walls. Two tall illuminated display windows with colored panels stand above a wooden desk, with red chairs and a carved ceiling visible.

Interior photograph from Sir John Soane’s Museum showing a densely arranged classical sculpture gallery. A central white male bust stands on a pedestal amid stone urns, small standing figures, carved architectural fragments, and shelves of busts and reliefs.

[[END OF PAGE 1]]

[[START OF PAGE 2]]

Exterior photograph of Sir John Soane’s Museum, showing a multi-story townhouse facade with a pale central section, arched ground-floor openings, and dark brick sections on either side.

This house is called
Sir John Soane’s Museum.

Sir John Soane lived here.

Portrait of Sir John Soane, shown as a seated man in dark clothing against a red background.

He was born in 1753 and died in
1837.

Photograph of a museum display with a tall ornate standing sculpture on a pedestal, surrounded by carved reliefs, busts, and other sculptural objects.

He liked to buy interesting things to keep in his house.

Three-panel collage of museum artifacts: a tall standing stone statue, a painting of a black dog on a cushioned seat, and a carved human head with an open mouth.

You can look at them in the
museum.

It is full of paintings, statues, and
lots more.

It is free to visit.

Everyone is welcome.

[[END OF PAGE 2]]

[[START OF PAGE 3]]

Clock pictogram showing the museum opening time 10:00 and closing time 5:00, with a green arrow between the two clocks.

# The museum is open from

## 10am to 5pm

Weekly museum opening schedule showing Monday and Sunday marked with red Xs and Tuesday through Saturday marked with green check marks.

from Tuesday to Saturday.

Museum-hours icon showing Sunday (“Su”) and Monday (“M”) marked with a red X, indicating the museum is closed on those days.

It is closed every Sunday and Monday and all bank holidays.

Street map locating the Soane Museum at 13 Lincoln’s Inn Fields, London WC2A 3BP. A red arrow points to the building marked “13” beside the museum label, near Remnant Street, Kingsway, and High Holborn; Holborn station and Lincoln’s Inn Fields are also shown.

[[END OF PAGE 3]]

[[START OF PAGE 4]]

Illustration of a bus stop with a red double-decker bus, a route sign showing 46, 22, and 5, a walking woman, and a stopwatch marked 15 minutes.

You can get there from Camden on the 46 bus.

Get off at the bus stop for
Chancery Lane.

It is a 15 minute walk from there.

Illustration of two people beside a train, with a stopwatch labeled "10" indicating a 10-minute walk to Holborn tube station.

## Holborn tube station is a

10 minute walk from the museum.

Photo of two adults standing side by side, accompanying the museum front-gate staff instruction.

There will be staff at the front gate to show you in to the museum.

Photo of an old lidded ceramic vessel displayed in a museum exhibit.

A lot of the things in the museum are very old.

We need to take good care of them.

Red X icon beside a digital camera, indicating that photos are not allowed.

We will ask you not to take photos.



0000 0000 0000

We will ask you to turn off your mobile phone.

[[END OF PAGE 4]]

[[START OF PAGE 5]]

We will ask you to put your bag into a plastic bag, or leave it with staff.

We will ask you not to touch the things in the museum.

If you are coming as a group, you will need to let us know.

Photo of a smiling man in a red hoodie holding a red corded telephone handset, illustrating the museum phone contact option.

You can ring the museum on
020 7440 4263.

Email contact icon showing a laptop screen with an envelope labeled "email".

You can email the museum on
admin@soane.org.uk

Photo of a small group gathered around a table with papers and small objects, illustrating a group visit or staff talk.

Your group can make a time with us to come for a talk by our staff.

Photo of a person seated in a wheelchair, accompanying the museum access note about a lift for wheelchair users.

If you use a wheelchair there is a lift outside to get into the museum.

[[END OF PAGE 5]]

[[START OF PAGE 6]]

Photo of a person in a wheelchair facing closed metal elevator doors, illustrating a museum lift.

There is a lift inside the museum. Staff will work the lifts for you.

We have 2 narrow wheelchairs for you to use inside the museum.

Photo of a smiling man in a red hoodie holding a red corded telephone handset, illustrating the instruction to call ahead so a wheelchair can be saved.

Please let us know you are coming so that we can save you a wheelchair.

Photo of a narrow museum corridor with red walls, display cases, and a dark passage ahead, illustrating narrow and dark rooms.

Some rooms in the museum are
very narrow.

Some rooms are dark.

Illustration of a man pointing at a floor surface with a raised step, accompanying the note that some museum rooms have floors that are not level.

Some rooms have floors that are
not level.

Accessibility illustration showing a person using a walking stick marked with a green check, and a red wheeled walking frame marked with a red X, indicating the stick is acceptable while the walking frame will not fit.

If you have a stick or crutches you can get around the museum but walking frames will not fit.

[[END OF PAGE 6]]

[[START OF PAGE 7]]

Portrait of Sir John Soane, showing a seated man in dark clothing against a red background.

# Who was Sir John Soane?

His job was to draw plans for new
buildings.

Collage of architectural drawings or watercolor views associated with Sir John Soane’s plans for the Bank of England, showing arched interiors, vaulted spaces, and a street view.

He made the plans for the Bank of
England.

Photo of a wall densely covered with framed paintings, including a large harbor scene, illustrating the page’s point that Sir John Soane bought many artworks.

He liked to spend his money on art.

Interior photograph of a densely furnished room, with arched openings, ornate wall decorations, and numerous sculptures, busts, and vessels.

He bought so many things that
there was no more room in his
house.

He bought the house next door and filled that up too,

Street-level photo of a row of multi-story townhouses, illustrating the page’s point that Sir John Soane bought adjoining houses.

so he bought the house next door to that as well.

[[END OF PAGE 7]]

[[START OF PAGE 8]]

Interior of a historic house museum, with framed paintings covering dark walls beneath a tall, ornate vaulted ceiling.

He wanted his house to be kept as a museum.

We keep it looking like it did when he lived there.

Ornate museum interior corridor with tall white columns, decorative ceiling details, and a bright doorway at the far end.

The museum has 4 floors.

There are 3 floors of rooms you can
visit.

Interior photo of a museum room with tall wooden bookshelves filled with books, decorative red walls, and upholstered seating.

All the rooms have lots of things to look at.

Ornate museum room interior with a round table, fireplace, wall mirrors, framed pictures, and a decorative domed ceiling.

Sir John had rooms for

• reading

• eating meals

• working

- meeting people

⚫ looking at pictures

[[END OF PAGE 8]]

[[START OF PAGE 9]]

Photo of a museum exhibit space with a large stone vessel or basin on column-like supports, surrounded by statues, columns, and arched alcoves.

On the bottom floor there is a dark space full of old statues, vases and coffins for mummies from Egyptian and Roman times.

The staff are happy to answer any
questions you have about the
museum.

There is a shop in the museum where you can buy something to remind you of your visit.

Two restroom accessibility pictograms: a separate women's and men's toilet sign and a wheelchair-accessible toilet sign.

There are toilets on the bottom
floor.

Cafe pictogram showing a cup of coffee and a plate of toast, labeled "Cafe".

There is a cafe in the park in front of the museum.

It is called the Fields Bar and
Kitchen.

[[END OF PAGE 9]]

[[START OF PAGE 10]]

Contact-themed photo of two adults holding red telephone handsets, split by a diagonal green-and-blue background.

# How to contact us

Photo of a person seated in a wheelchair, used with the wheelchair booking/access contact information.

to book a wheelchair

or ask about any other access

Phone

000
000

email

020 7405 2107
admin@soane.org.uk

Photo of four adults gathered around a table with papers and small objects, illustrating the learning activities contact option.

to take part in learning activities

Phone

000
000
000

020 7440 4247

email

caidoo@soane.org.uk



to book a time for a group visit

Phone
000
000

000

020 7405 2107

email

admin@soane.org.uk

Logo for Sir John Soane's Museum London, with the text "The Advocacy Project" and a blue/yellow person icon.

Photo of a person holding an open easy-read book labeled "easy read" and "Easy words and pictures."

This leaflet was made
easy to read by the
Camden easy info team
at the Advocacy Project

with
made photo
symbols

[[END OF PAGE 10]]
